head: 6e4be86902742aef4f9b488143d8693db858e1b9
claim: A cloud app that saves copies of a Boat computer sees the copy from before an update listed as before-update and still there after pruning, while ordinary copies are pruned to the newest few

steps.start: Clean worktree on fm/byk-cloud-undo-2 with dependencies installed; no cloud machine, copy or account existed. The consumer started from an empty loopback Boat bench (startFakeSandboxServer) with an in-memory store.
steps: Built the workspace SDK with npm run build (exit 0).
Wrote a Node consumer in a scratch folder that imports only @byokit/cloud and @byokit/cloud/testing, and ran it.
Created a machine named web with keepCopies, and a second machine named web-two whose copy must not be touched; saved a copy of web for web-two.
Wrote a marker file, saved a copy, changed the marker, and restored the copy; read the marker back and checked the new machine id, that the old machine was gone, and that the machine was on.
Took three more ordinary copies, then saved one more with keep 1; listed the copies after each step.
Saved a copy named as before an update (undo prefix) on web, then saved two more ordinary copies with keep 1; listed the copies with their kind.
Deleted the before-update copy and ran the scheduled copy with keep 1 until its first check reported a copy.
Restored a copy id that does not exist to see the error, and printed its words; ran disk() with a scripted df output and printed the usage words.
steps.result: The printed output shows the copy saved before the update with kind before-update, still listed after pruning with keep 1 (the other copy listed with no kind is the single newest ordinary copy kept); ordinary copies were pruned to the newest one at keep 1 and to three before that; the other machine's copy was kept; the missing copy error read 'That saved copy of your cloud computer is gone. Choose another one.'; disk showed 3.3 GB of 12.9 GB used.
